claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925, gpt-tokenizer 4.0.0 was qualified to replace the pinned 3.4.0 as the o200k_base counter behind this repository's exact-count instruments (tools/token-report/token_manifest.py count_files and compare, and scripts/recount-tokens.cjs). The Gate A condition was that o200k counts be identical on every retained artifact pair under both versions and that token_manifest.py compare output be unchanged; a scout passed it and an independent verifier reproduced every condition. All 47 distinct artifacts retained in the host's token-report ledger (25 comparison rows) counted identically under 3.4.0 and 4.0.0, with identical full token arrays, and equal to their recorded tokens (3,032,861 in total). Running token_manifest.py compare over all 25 retained pairs, once with the origin/main script on 3.4.0 and once with the same script changed only in its two version literals on 4.0.0, gave identical CLI output and ledger payloads for 25 of 25, and each comparison_id equalled its ledger row id. Special-token and edge-case probes behaved the same under both versions. The upstream suite at tag 4.0.0 exited 0: vp check found all 58 files formatted and no warnings, lint or type errors in 47, and vitest passed 6 of 6 test files and 1,376 of 1,376 tests. The pass covers default encode of encoding/o200k_base on UTF-8 text under Node v24.21.0.
limitations: Scope: default encode of cjs/encoding/o200k_base.js, also reached as the gpt-tokenizer/encoding/o200k_base subpath, on UTF-8 text under Node v24.21.0. The allowedSpecial and disallowedSpecial modes were checked only on the 22 special-token literals. Model-name entry points (gpt-2 now maps to the new gpt2 encoding), o200k_harmony, gpt2 and the dist/ UMD bundles that 4.0.0 removed are not qualified.

The retained corpus contains no BOM, CRLF, special-token or non-UTF-8 text. Those cases rest on synthetic probes, 30,000 seeded random strings and 12,000 artifact-slice variants, which are randomized, not exhaustive.

Ledger comparison ids and payloads do not record the tokenizer version (the key is tool, the two sha256 values, encoding and boundary), so rows counted under 3.4.0 and 4.0.0 cannot be told apart. That is safe only because the counts are identical; every future bump must be re-qualified the same way.

The version guards at tools/token-report/token_manifest.py L162 and scripts/recount-tokens.cjs L14 do not contain the string 'gpt-tokenizer'. A bump found only by searching for the package name misses them and leaves the new version rejected with 'Pinned tokenizer version mismatch'.

The upstream suite ran the tag's source, not the published 4.0.0 tarball, because CI's 'vp run build' step was not run; its other deviations are in data.upstream_suite.deviations. The verifier's re-run reused the scout's yarn install. The published tarballs were covered by the differential checks instead.

Registry integrity (npm view dist.integrity against the package-lock) was checked by the scout only; the verifier re-read the scout's retained output and did not query the registry. Hashes, integrity values and commit ids in data are prefixes as the gate results recorded them: 16 hex characters for file sha256 values and the upstream clone head, 16 characters after 'sha512-' for integrity values, 12 for the task base, 8 for the scout's origin/main and 16 for the verifier's. catalog_revision is the full 40-character commit.

4.0.0 is a full toolchain rebuild: of 1,348 files in the 3.4.0 package, 1,145 changed, and 4.0.0 adds 380 files and drops 191, including the dist/ UMD bundles and the shipped test files. Behavior was equal on everything tested, but the changed surface is large.

Under both versions BPE slows sharply on long unspaced CJK or emoji text: a 60,000-character CJK chunk took about 7.6 s under 3.4.0 and 6.3 s under 4.0.0. count_files counts every path in one node call with a 30 s timeout, so inputs like that could time out under either version.
blueprints/us-equities/research-runtime/measure_packet.cjs was not exercised because it needs a LEAN results input; it keeps its 3.4.0 pin together with its dated receipt.

At qualification the host's private token-report configuration pointed at a 3.4.0 package. Once the 4.0.0 pin lands, count_files rejects that installation with 'Pinned tokenizer version mismatch' until the host installation is switched to 4.0.0; this receipt records no host installation change.

The host's token-report-refresh.service rewrote the real state directory during the verification (2026-09-29T03:09:02Z to 03:09:37Z per journalctl): new captures, ledger snapshots and native events, and one comparison's last_seen. The scout's own no-writes check for its session could not be repeated.

The upstream release notes and the 3.4.0...4.0.0 comparison were read over the network with gh because the scratch upstream clone was shallow and lacked tag 3.4.0; that part is source reading, not execution.

The scout's exact counts for its BOM, 200,000-character and CJK probes could not be checked because its probe strings were not retained; the verifier's own probes reproduced its same-result verdicts with different strings and counts.
gpt-tokenizer is not a manifests/stack.json component, so this receipt names no component_ids and has no manifests/evidence.json receipts[] entry; it is registered in files[] only.

Both scratch ledgers held 29 identical rows (25 retained plus 4 successful synthetic pairs).

CLI JSON was identical for 25 of 25, and per field for baseline, candidate, comparison_id, provider_tokens_saved, semantic_acceptance and tokens_removed (25 each). Scratch ledger payloads were identical for 25 of 25 and matched the real rows on tool, encoding, boundary, tokens_removed and sha256, bytes and tokens.

CI's 'vp run build' step was not run, so the suite exercised the tag's source, not the published 4.0.0 tarball.
The upstream AGENTS.md L10 says tests or internet commands need escalated permissions; the sandbox was not overridden, and no network-dependent test skipped or failed.
